If f(x) = 0 has exactly five distinct roots in (a, b), then g(x)g'(x) = 0 has at least :
questions.explanation:
f′(x) = g(x)

f′'(x) = g'(x)

Given, g(x).g'(x) = 0

f′(x).f′'(x) = 0

Also given f(x) has exactly 5 roots.

So from Rolle's theorem we can say,

f′(x) has 4 roots and f′'(x) has 3 roots.

f′(x).f′'(x) = 0 has 4 + 3 = 7 roots.
